[QUERENT] Crowd Counting Consortium

[SYSTEM] The Crowd Counting Consortium (CCC) is a joint research project that tracks and collects public data on political protests, marches, rallies, strikes, and acts of civil disobedience across the United States. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHrOzAV8kN1TO5Yh85LFJ5h5lUSDPjWobOBjAFOTuPAzR_uI7KN5RCKDEf5TGgbWj1Q6x9wlVxIuZwAuPVpq55a45Gw9bZefOrq9uTif1jMmUgZNeBg5Pzv3HJrQpwQDxmeGXMnCjLBCagYorHv0yT63KQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEB6zswFfSlmKyGJ2KX4jWwoV7H-JEWtuTCb_lNCKVTi9i-apDFsUdB_5CzDINScyvirme01Asewc5KTfo0Wyp11QLqWX0P_vvsXhL3zYq9ClGSJ_Gr4fULuWpO2dWpMbthGl7dh0YkNDs29GTyLUpMZdS4gQovbDOfiSnpa5v46i_na_-wUIct)]
Key Details

* Leadership & Origin: Co-founded in 2017 by Erica Chenoweth (Harvard University) and Jeremy Pressman (University of Connecticut) following the Women's March on Washington. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHrOzAV8kN1TO5Yh85LFJ5h5lUSDPjWobOBjAFOTuPAzR_uI7KN5RCKDEf5TGgbWj1Q6x9wlVxIuZwAuPVpq55a45Gw9bZefOrq9uTif1jMmUgZNeBg5Pzv3HJrQpwQDxmeGXMnCjLBCagYorHv0yT63KQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEB6zswFfSlmKyGJ2KX4jWwoV7H-JEWtuTCb_lNCKVTi9i-apDFsUdB_5CzDINScyvirme01Asewc5KTfo0Wyp11QLqWX0P_vvsXhL3zYq9ClGSJ_Gr4fULuWpO2dWpMbthGl7dh0YkNDs29GTyLUpMZdS4gQovbDOfiSnpa5v46i_na_-wUIct)]
* Institutional Home: Operated in partnership with the [Nonviolent Action Lab](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHrOzAV8kN1TO5Yh85LFJ5h5lUSDPjWobOBjAFOTuPAzR_uI7KN5RCKDEf5TGgbWj1Q6x9wlVxIuZwAuPVpq55a45Gw9bZefOrq9uTif1jMmUgZNeBg5Pzv3HJrQpwQDxmeGXMnCjLBCagYorHv0yT63KQ) at the Harvard Kennedy School’s Ash Center for Democratic Governance and Innovation. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHrOzAV8kN1TO5Yh85LFJ5h5lUSDPjWobOBjAFOTuPAzR_uI7KN5RCKDEf5TGgbWj1Q6x9wlVxIuZwAuPVpq55a45Gw9bZefOrq9uTif1jMmUgZNeBg5Pzv3HJrQpwQDxmeGXMnCjLBCagYorHv0yT63KQ)]
* Scope: Systematically logs public, nonviolent (and broader political) crowd events across all U.S. states and territories with no minimum size requirement. This includes historic movements such as the 2017 Women's March, 2018 March for Our Lives, 2020 Black Lives Matter protests, campus encampments, and subsequent political demonstrations. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWgHrOzAVg5LY1B-6Ws7G8oEkIf675mhVtLnEXZzHaVlGGGsQy13xQUyRQVbcpizUhMrRa47A6POift2AJm6_1IbXjnrBSxygc9Pc7O2jXwtR5b7gHFvDemT6RA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAVQKxivcpf7Y7O0njXXE4Iw6Y5mvtzO9wGguOoMtJOujC4be_lw6BP7ROvkpr7REE35f0UktAY4letclLQ45SoKsXEP3lN19X0y9006CCu8C80WAEMICxgF4pwDp8B0A7OaZD6), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHrOzAV8kN1TO5Yh85LFJ5h5lUSDPjWobOBjAFOTuPAzR_uI7KN5RCKDEf5TGgbWj1Q6x9wlVxIuZwAuPVpq55a45Gw9bZefOrq9uTif1jMmUgZNeBg5Pzv3HJrQpwQDxmeGXMnCjLBCagYorHv0yT63KQ)]
* Scale: The project has tracked hundreds of thousands of individual demonstrations and rallies across the U.S. since 2017. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUwHrOzAVDuDllU3GNIjzsyj_WQCJzvKHG5lzfa4am5peE4Y2vq4yza3KuA09e4qz4rQMjdjGx9PzHQkOQkigaFrDve5YrIeZwb7DQS3BDzTSmQOf)]

Accessing the Data

* Monthly Data: Published regularly on Harvard Dataverse. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHrOzAV8kN1TO5Yh85LFJ5h5lUSDPjWobOBjAFOTuPAzR_uI7KN5RCKDEf5TGgbWj1Q6x9wlVxIuZwAuPVpq55a45Gw9bZefOrq9uTif1jMmUgZNeBg5Pzv3HJrQpwQDxmeGXMnCjLBCagYorHv0yT63KQ)]
* Weekly/Compiled Updates: A compiled and augmented version of the dataset is updated weekly on Wednesdays via the Nonviolent Action Lab GitHub Repository. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWQHrOzAVXTIP9tfHF_0FOMCLBoCXrH3ye6nAmQSoMCR-cX3y5nqMPPdwbNedaRUjvciVGY64IK2wzkqsVbVs5F-kun9u-Zm1-3_8VtAKzkGUf2ZPXbx00zRF)]
* Interactive Tools: You can explore data visuals and project updates directly through the [Counting Crowds Website](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWQHrOzAVXTIP9tfHF_0FOMCLBoCXrH3ye6nAmQSoMCR-cX3y5nqMPPdwbNedaRUjvciVGY64IK2wzkqsVbVs5F-kun9u-Zm1-3_8VtAKzkGUf2ZPXbx00zRF). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWQHrOzAVXTIP9tfHF_0FOMCLBoCXrH3ye6nAmQSoMCR-cX3y5nqMPPdwbNedaRUjvciVGY64IK2wzkqsVbVs5F-kun9u-Zm1-3_8VtAKzkGUf2ZPXbx00zRF)]

transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: THE CONSORTIUM, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Crowd Counting Consortium (CCC) is a joint research project that tracks and collects public data on political protests, marches, rallies, strikes, and acts of civil disobedience across the United States.' Founders, home, scope, scale, data access. Six cards: Harvard, Counting Crowds (two), boB Rudis, Policy Commons, X.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the consortium, the Overview gives its founders, institutional home, scope and data.
findings: THE SCOPE WITH A NARROWING AND AN ADDITION. 'Systematically logs public, nonviolent (and broader political) crowd events'. The consortium's page: 'We collect publicly available data on political crowds reported in the United States'. 'nonviolent' is on card 3's page, a third party's description of the dataset ('nonviolent (not primarily organized to cause direct harm to persons)'). 'strikes' in the composition's definition is on no card. 'hundreds of thousands of individual demonstrations' stands beside the consortium's own count of 200,000 protests and rallies (its X account, card 6).

THE RULES NOT CARRIED. 'We only post records that we can confirm and verify through fact-checking.' and 'We will never post, release, or share identifying information that has not already been reported in the public' (the consortium's page).
analysis: Faithful on founders, home and data. The composition puts a third party's 'nonviolent' first in a scope the consortium states without it, adds strikes, and leaves out the verification and privacy rules that bound the record.
per_note: Founders and institutions named; the consortium's pages among the cards.
